compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX 5090 Mobile (Blackwell): tensor cores prefer fp16 MMA with K%16==0; C=32 is small; MLP hidden=128. Use tl.dot for big GEMM (B*nH*nW*N x C).
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Attention is tiny per window (N=16, C=32). Bulk compute is in MLP (BHW * 32 -> 128 -> 32) and qkv/proj linears. These linears dominate flops.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Small inner dims may underutilize tensor cores; need careful tiling.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input tensor is 1x720x1280x32 fp16 = ~58MB. MLP hidden activation = ~232MB. Bandwidth-bound MLP. Fuse LN+Linear and activation+Linear where possible.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Materializing fc1 output (4x size) wastes BW; consider fusing fc1+gelu+fc2 if hidden tile fits in regs.

register_pressure.notes: C=32 small enough to keep entire row in registers. Hidden=128 OK per row. Fused MLP per token feasible.
register_pressure.risk: Fully fusing fc1+gelu+fc2 per tile requires hidden=128 register tile.

nodes.notes: PROBLEM: Swin block (single-head, no shift) on fp16 input (1,720,1280,32). Wh=Ww=4, N=16 per window, nH=180, nW=320, Bw=57600 windows. CLASSIFICATION: composite kernel = LN + qkv-linear + per-window attention (softmax) + proj-linear + residual + LN + fc1(32->128) + GELU + fc2(128->32) + residual. DATA SHAPES: x (B=1,H=720,W=1280,C=32) fp16, qkv W (96,32), proj W (32,32), fc1 W (128,32), fc2 W (32,128), rpe (1,1,16,16). DEPENDENCIES: per-token LN reduces over C=32; attention reduces over N=16; MLP reduces over 32 then 128. REGIMES: (a) full BHW (921600 tokens) - bandwidth bound; (b) per-window attention - tiny GEMM N=16,C=32 - latency bound; (c) MLP fc1->fc2 - bw bound on hidden activation. DOMINANT COSTS: fc1 (BHW*32*128) + fc2 (BHW*128*32) ~ 2*3.7GFLOP each; attention small. STRATEGY: 1) fuse LN1+qkv into a single kernel writing (Bw,N,3C); 2) attention kernel per window (16x16 attn matrix, easy in shared); 3) fuse proj + residual + LN2; 4) fuse fc1+gelu+fc2+residual (hidden 128 fits in registers per row). KNOBS: tile rows per program, vectorization, dtype of accumulators (fp32), pre-pack weights. OPEN ACTIONS proposed below.

action.description: Implement a fused Triton kernel for LayerNorm1 + qkv matmul: read x (B,H,W,C), compute mean/var across C in fp32, apply LN with weight/bias, multiply by qkv_weight (3C x C) and add qkv_bias, write Q,K,V tiles laid out per-window for the attention step. Token-parallel grid; each program handles BLOCK_M tokens. Keep C=32 fully in registers.
action.rationale: Eliminates one full read/write pass over x. C=32 is tiny, ideal for register-resident reduction. qkv is a small GEMM that fuses cheaply.
action.title: Fuse LN1 + QKV linear into one kernel

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: qkv: out=96, in=32 -> tl.dot with K=32 (multiple of 16 OK). Tiny K may underutilize tensor cores; pad/broadcast for throughput.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Compute is small relative to memory; fusing reduces BW dominantly.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Tensor-core efficiency at K=32 modest; may need to batch many rows.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Saves one read+write of the BHW*C tensor vs separate LN and Linear kernels.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Need proper layout to enable coalesced writes to (Bw,N,3C).

register_pressure.notes: Per-row registers: 32 inputs + 96 outputs partial accumulators ~ fine.
register_pressure.risk: If BLOCK_M too large, register spill.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: Alternative to doing LN and qkv separately. Cannot combine with n2/n3 trivially since they target later stages; but composes with them in a full plan.

action.description: Single Triton kernel that, per window (Bw=57600 windows, N=16, C=32), loads Q,K,V (already produced), computes attn=QK^T*scale + rpe, softmax along last dim, then attn@V, then applies proj (32x32) + bias, and adds the residual x_input. Output: (B,H,W,C). Each program handles one window.
action.rationale: Whole attention block fits comfortably in shared memory/registers (16x32 tiles). Fusing proj and residual avoids extra passes.
action.title: Fused window-attention + proj + residual kernel

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: QK^T: 16x32 @ 32x16 -> 16x16; softmax across 16; AV: 16x16 @ 16x32 -> 16x32; proj: 16x32 @ 32x32. All tiles fit MMA shape constraints (multiples of 16).
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Plenty of compute reuse per window; mostly compute/latency-bound at tiny size.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: 57600 programs each tiny; kernel launch and per-program overhead might dominate. Consider grouping multiple windows per program.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Reads QKV once, writes output once; loads proj weight once per program (broadcastable).
memory_bandwidth.risk: proj weight reloaded per program unless cached.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: Alternative grouping vs splitting attention/proj into separate kernels. Distinct from n1 (pre-attention) and n3 (MLP), composes with them.

action.description: Fuse LayerNorm2 + fc1(32->128) + GELU + fc2(128->32) + residual into one per-token kernel. Each program handles BLOCK_M tokens. Keep the 128-dim hidden activation entirely in registers (no global write of 4x activation). Use tl.dot for both linears with weights loaded from global per program (or cached via constexpr).
action.rationale: MLP dominates BW. Avoiding materialization of the hidden=128 activation saves ~232MB of traffic. Hidden=128 fits in registers per row.
action.title: Fuse LN2 + FC1 + GELU + FC2 + residual

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: fc1: K=32 (small); fc2: K=128. Both multiples of 16 OK for MMA. tl.dot tiles of (BLOCK_M,128) and (BLOCK_M,32) typical.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: K=32 underutilizes mma vs K=128, but BLOCK_M big enough to amortize.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Eliminates a full hidden tensor pass; saves the biggest BW cost in the block.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Weights for fc1 (4KB) and fc2 (8KB) are small; reload OK or use constexpr.

register_pressure.notes: BLOCK_M=64 with hidden=128 = 8192 fp16/fp32 regs per program; needs care.
register_pressure.risk: Possible spills if BLOCK_M too large. Tune BLOCK_M.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: Alternative to splitting MLP into 2 kernels; cannot trivially combine with siblings because they target different stages, but composes with n1/n2 in the full plan.

action.description: As a faster bring-up alternative: keep PyTorch linears (or fp16 cublas) for qkv/proj/fc1/fc2 but write fused Triton kernels for (a) LN+input prep, (b) per-window attention softmax, (c) GELU fused with residual add. Lower risk; smaller wins but quick correctness.
action.rationale: De-risks correctness path; provides baseline to compare deeper fusions against torch.compile.
action.title: Minimal fusion baseline (LN + softmax + GELU only)

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Relies on cublas for GEMMs; no MMA tuning needed.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: May not beat torch.compile which also fuses LN+GELU.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Some saving on LN and GELU passes only.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: This is an alternative bring-up plan vs deep fusion (n1+n2+n3). Cannot run simultaneously with the full-fusion path as the primary plan; choose one direction first.

kernel_summary: Simplified Swin block in fp16: LN1 -> QKV linear -> per-window single-head attention (window 4x4, N=16, C=32) with relative position bias -> proj linear + residual -> LN2 -> MLP (32->128->32) with GELU + residual. Input is (1,720,1280,32) fp16, with 57,600 windows. Dominant costs are the MLP linears (BW-bound on the 128-dim hidden activation) and the qkv/proj linears; per-window attention is tiny and latency-prone. Constraints: C=32 (small K), MMA needs multiples of 16 (all OK), num_heads=1, no shift. Plan: fuse LN1+QKV, fuse attention+proj+residual per window, and most importantly fuse LN2+FC1+GELU+FC2+residual to keep the 128-dim hidden activation in registers and avoid a 4x memory blow-up.
open_questions: What BLOCK_M maximizes throughput for the fused LN2+MLP kernel without register spilling on RTX 5090 Mobile?
Is it faster to group multiple windows per Triton program for the attention kernel, or one window per program?
Should weights (qkv/proj/fc1/fc2) be pre-transposed/packed for better tl.dot layout (e.g., (in,out) vs (out,in))?
Will tl.dot with K=32 on Blackwell tensor cores be efficient enough, or should we use mma-friendly K accumulation tricks?
Does torch.compile already fuse LN+Linear/GELU competitively, raising the bar we need to beat?
Are fp16 accumulations in attention safe within tolerance, or must softmax/qk be in fp32?
Is the rpe_bias broadcast (1,1,N,N) handled cheaply via shared/constant memory?
Can we avoid the window partition reshape entirely by indexing tokens via (b,nh,wh,nw,ww,c) directly in the kernel?
